title: Explainable Outlier Detection for Interval-valued Data
summary: Outlier detection for interval-valued data has lacked an explanation layer. The paper derives closed-form Shapley values and a Shapley interaction index for the squared robust Interval-Mahalanobis distance under the IMCD estimator, decomposing outlyingness into centers, ranges, and cross-terms. On the Cars and Spotify datasets it illustrates variable-level explanations and flags outliers consistent with domain knowledge.

claims.metric: number of observations flagged as outliers

match_target.why: C1 is the cheapest claim that still tests the paper's central result: on the tiny 27x4 Cars data, the reweighted IMCD plus 0.9 farness cutoff must reproduce the five Figure 1 outlier flags; the Shapley figures depend on the same robust fit.

tolerance.why: Rule 3 applies: no repeated-run std is reported and this is not a 2,000+ test-set percentage; the outlier count is bounded on the small 27-observation set, so use 2.0 absolute points, while also checking the exact five labels qualitatively against Figure 1.

requirements.stmt: Represent each interval by its center c=(a+b)/2 and range r=b-a; for Cars use the uniform microdata distribution because no microdata are available.
requirements.quote: since no microdata are available, assuming a continuous uniform distribution for the latent variables

requirements.stmt: Apply a logarithmic transform to Price only; retain EngCap, Top Speed, and Acceleration as interval variables.
requirements.quote: applying a logarithmic transformation to the Price variable (denoted as lnPrice)

requirements.stmt: Use the 27 Cars observations and four interval-valued variables; the class variable is not part of the distance computation.
requirements.quote: It is composed of 27 observations corresponding to different car models, with four interval-valued variables

requirements.stmt: Estimate the barycenter and symbolic covariance matrix with the reweighted IMCD algorithm using an approximately 75% subset and farness cutoff 0.9.
requirements.quote: with a subset of approximately 75% of the total observations and a farness cutoff of 0.9

requirements.stmt: Compute the squared robust Interval-Mahalanobis distance using Definition 3.1/Equation (5) with the robust barycenter and robust symbolic covariance matrix.
requirements.quote: a robust version of the Interval-Mahalanobis distance can be obtained by using the robust estimates of the barycenter and symbolic covariance matrix

requirements.stmt: Convert squared distances to farness outlier scores by median/MAD standardization, robust Yeo-Johnson transformation, second median/MAD standardization, and Normal-CDF scoring.
requirements.quote: the squared distances are standardized using the median and the median absolute deviation (MAD)

requirements.stmt: Flag observations whose farness outlier score exceeds 0.9; for Cars this is the reported cutoff.
requirements.quote: observations with an outlier score exceeding this threshold are flagged as outliers

requirements.stmt: Compute Shapley values with the closed-form expression in Theorem 4.1/Corollary 4.2 and verify the efficiency property numerically.
requirements.quote: the sum of the Shapley values of all variables equals the squared Interval-Mahalanobis distance of the observation to the barycenter

requirements.stmt: For Cars, because the latent variables are symmetric and identically distributed, set Psi=0 and the cross center-range Shapley terms to zero; report the center and range decomposition in Figure 3a.
requirements.quote: Since we assumed symmetric and identically distributed latent variables, the cross centers-ranges contributions are zero

requirements.stmt: Produce the Figure 2a barplot for the top six Cars observations by descending distance, including Bmwserie7 even though it is not flagged.
requirements.quote: only the six observations with the largest distances are shown, ordered from greatest to smallest distance

requirements.stmt: Implement the Shapley interaction index with off-diagonal terms from Equation (10) and diagonal terms defined so that each Shapley value is the row sum; reproduce the Ferrari tile plot in Figure 3b.

data.how_to_get: Install the CRAN package MAINT.Data (version 2.8.0 is cited) and load the Cars interval data; the AIDA repository also includes raw-data and the Shapley examples vignette.
